title: Bioprinting of Cartilage and Skin Tissue Analogs Utilizing a Novel Passive Mixing Unit Technique for Bioink Precellularization
protocol: Prepare two syringes, one for the cell suspension and one for the bioink.
Couple a sterile passive mixing unit with dual syringes via Luer lock connection.
Obtain a dispensing unit capable of extruding volumes from two sterile syringes simultaneously at a controlled rate.
Use a 12 mL syringe for bioink and a 1 mL syringe for cell suspension to achieve a 10:1 mixing ratio.
Prepare a sterile cartridge and a sterile female-female Luer lock connector for direct mixing of bioink and cell suspension.
Obtain or prepare the nanocellulose/alginate based bioink for blending with cells.
Detach cells using a 0.5% trypsin/EDTA solution.
Count total number of cells using the trypan blue exclusion method.
Determine the desired final cell density in the printed construct.
Calculate the concentration of harvested cells needed to achieve the target final cell density.
Select a desired cell concentration for experiments: Ccell (cells/mL).
Calculate the volume of bioink necessary based on the total number of constructs desired: Vbioink = Vconstruct × NConstructs.
Calculate the number of cells needed: Ncells = Ccell × 1.1 × Vbiolink.
Resuspend the cells in a volume that is 1/10th of the bioink volume: Vcell suspension = 0.1 × Vbiolink.
Transfer the cell suspension into the cell suspension syringe.
Transfer the bioink to another syringe or obtain a syringe containing the bioink.
Pull back the plunger of the bioink syringe and insert it into the dispensing unit with the Luer lock connector upwards.
Pull back the plunger of the cell syringe to a similar length as the bioink syringe and insert it into the dispensing unit.
Attach both syringes to the mixing unit by twisting the Luer lock connectors.
Prime the mixing system by pushing on the dispensing unit to extrude air in the syringe.
Attach the filling cartridge to the end of the mixing unit via the Luer lock connector after priming.
Compress the dispensing unit slowly to mix bioink and cell suspension together into the cartridge.
Push the plunger in the filling cartridge downward with a sterile pipet tip to contact the bioink-cell mixture.
Cap the cartridge and gently tap on the work surface to move air bubbles to the top of the cartridge.
Blend cells into the bioink using the passive mixing unit technique 1, 2, or 3 times prior to dispensing into a mold for cross-linking using 100 mM CaCl2.
Mix the cell/bioink directly into a syringe rather than a cartridge if performing additional blends.
Remix the blend through the mixing unit without the cell syringe component after mixing directly in a syringe.
Blend cells into a separate bioink using manual mechanical mixing via a spatula for durations of 30, 60, or 90 seconds.
Transfer the mixtures to a mold for cross-linking using 100 mM CaCl2.
Transfer samples to a well plate after completing the cross-linking process and culture under standard conditions.
Wash the constructs in serum-free cell culture medium for 30 minutes after one day of culture.
Stain cells in the constructs with a staining solution containing 4 µM Calcein AM and 1 µM Ethidium homodimer-1 for 30 minutes.
Wash the samples two additional times.
Incubate the samples in serum-free cell culture medium at 37 °C for a total of one hour.
Transfer the samples to a live cell imaging solution.
Acquire images via a digital color camera at 10X magnification using an inverted microscope with FITC and Texas Red filters.
Analyze images using image analysis software.
Randomly select three images from each construct for quantification of cell viability.
Calculate cell viability based on the ratio of live cells to total number of cells.
Analyze the data via one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's multiple comparisons test.
Draw a 3D model of the desired tissue analog.
Convert the 3D model to a Gcode file for bioprinting.
Load the Gcode file on the bioprinter.
Isolate and cryopreserve primary human nasal chondrocytes (hNC) from patients.
Thaw cryopreserved hNCs and expand them once in monolayer culture using standard culture medium at 37 °C.
Detach cells at 80 - 90% confluence with a 0.5% trypsin/EDTA solution.
Count the detached cells using a trypan blue exclusion protocol.
Conduct all experiments using hNCs at passage 2.
Resuspend hNCs at a concentration of 100 x 10^6 cells/mL in 300 μL of culture medium.
Supplement the culture medium with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 50 µg/mL ascorbic acid.
Blend the hNC cell suspension into a nanocellulose/alginate based bioink at a 10:1 ratio of bioink to cell suspension.
Sterilize the bioprinter via UV exposure.
Wipe down the bioprinter with 70% ethanol.
Place the bioprinter in a laminar flow cabinet to maintain sterility.
Attach sterile printing nozzles to the cartridges containing the bioink/cell suspension blends.
Insert the nozzles into the bioprinter.
Calibrate the bioprinter either manually or according to specific printer protocols.
Bioprint lattice-structured, cell-laden constructs using a 25G conical nozzle at a pressure of 25 kPa.
Bioprint cell-free constructs as controls.
Cross-link the constructs by adding an ionic solution of 100 mM CaCl2 for 5 minutes.
Rinse the constructs and incubate in culture medium under standard conditions (37 °C, 5% CO2, 95% relative humidity).
Change the media every second or third day.
Collect samples at weeks 2 and 4 for histological analysis.
Stain the samples for GAG production using an Alcian blue stain.
Draw a 3D model of the desired tissue analog.
Convert the 3D model to a Gcode file for bioprinting.
Load the Gcode file on the bioprinter.
Obtain primary HDF.
Maintain primary HDF in DMEM growth media supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 50 µg/mL ascorbic acid.
Detach primary HDF at 80 - 90% confluence with a 0.5% trypsin/EDTA solution.
Count detached primary HDF cells.
Isolate and cryopreserve primary hNC from patients following the referenced protocol.
Thaw and expand cryopreserved hNCs in monolayer culture.
Detach hNCs at 80 - 90% confluence with a 0.5% trypsin/EDTA solution.
Count detached hNC cells.
Resuspend both primary HDF and hNC cell types at 100 x 10^6 cells/mL within growth media.
Mix the cell suspensions together at a 1:1 ratio to achieve a final total concentration of 100 x 10^6 cells/mL in 300 µL of media.
Blend the 50:50 cell suspension of HDF and hNC into a nanocellulose/alginate based bioink following the passive mixing unit protocol.
Ensure that the bioprinter is sterilized or is placed in a laminar flow cabinet to maintain sterility.
Attach sterile printing nozzles to the cartridges containing the bioink/cell suspension blends and insert into the bioprinter.
Calibrate the bioprinter either manually or according to printer protocols.
Bioprint lattice-structured, cell-laden constructs using 25G conical nozzle at a pressure of 25 kPa.
Bioprint cell-free constructs as a control.
Cross-link the constructs by adding an ionic solution of 100 mM CaCl2 for 5 min.
Rinse the constructs and incubate in culture medium under standard conditions (37 °C, 5% CO2, and 95% relative humidity).
Change the media every second or third day.
Collect samples for histological analysis at weeks 2 and 4.
Stain the samples for collagen I production using a Masson's trichrome stain.
